# Best Practice Quality Checklist

This comprehensive checklist ensures that best practices meet enterprise architecture standards for quality, completeness, and practical applicability. All items must be addressed before a best practice can be approved and published.
page_texts.3:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#basic-metadata-requirements]

### Basic Metadata Requirements

- [ ] Best practice ID follows convention: `BP-{DOMAIN}-{TYPE}-{NNN}`
- [ ] Best practice name clearly describes the practice scope and focus
- [ ] Domain is correctly specified from approved taxonomy
- [ ] Practice type accurately reflects the nature of the practice
- [ ] Version follows semantic versioning (major.minor.patch)
- [ ] Status accurately reflects current state (draft, review, approved, published, deprecated)
- [ ] Maturity level accurately represents practice validation (emerging, proven, industry-standard)
- [ ] Tags are relevant, consistent with taxonomy, and support discoverability
- [ ] All metadata fields are properly formatted and complete
page_texts.4:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#document-structure-and-organization]

### Document Structure and Organization

- [ ] Document follows the approved best practice template structure
- [ ] All required sections are present and properly ordered
- [ ] Headers follow consistent markdown formatting standards
- [ ] Table of contents is accurate and comprehensive (if included)
- [ ] Cross-references and internal links are functional and accurate
- [ ] Document navigation is logical and user-friendly
- [ ] Content is properly organized within each section
- [ ] Section lengths are appropriate for content complexity
page_texts.6:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#executive-summary-assessment]

### Executive Summary Assessment

- [ ] Purpose statement clearly articulates what the practice addresses
- [ ] Business value is compelling and quantified where possible
- [ ] Benefits are specific, measurable, and achievable
- [ ] Strategic value demonstrates clear organizational impact
- [ ] Target audience is clearly defined and appropriate
- [ ] Scope and applicability are precisely described
- [ ] Scope boundaries explicitly define what is included/excluded
- [ ] Summary provides complete understanding without requiring full document reading
page_texts.7:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#practice-context-and-background]

### Practice Context and Background

- [ ] Business context clearly establishes need and strategic alignment
- [ ] Business drivers are specific and well-documented
- [ ] Strategic alignment demonstrates clear organizational value
- [ ] Technical context accurately describes environment and constraints
- [ ] Current state assessment is realistic and comprehensive
- [ ] Technical enablers are clearly identified and achievable
- [ ] Problem statement specifically describes challenges being addressed
- [ ] Impact assessment quantifies consequences of not implementing practice
- [ ] Success evidence demonstrates proven effectiveness across multiple implementations
- [ ] Quantified outcomes are credible and well-documented
page_texts.8:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#core-practice-description]

### Core Practice Description

- [ ] Practice overview provides comprehensive understanding of the approach
- [ ] Practice definition is clear, unambiguous, and actionable
- [ ] Practice components are well-defined and logically organized
- [ ] Key principles are fundamental to practice success
- [ ] Principles include clear description, rationale, and application guidance
- [ ] Core components are essential and sufficient for practice implementation
- [ ] Each component includes purpose, description, implementation, and success criteria
- [ ] Success criteria are measurable and achievable
- [ ] Practice description enables practical implementation
page_texts.9:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#implementation-methodology]

### Implementation Methodology

- [ ] Implementation approach is systematic and practical
- [ ] Methodology overview provides clear philosophical foundation
- [ ] Implementation lifecycle is logical and achievable
- [ ] Prerequisites are comprehensive and realistic
- [ ] Organizational prerequisites address leadership, structure, and capabilities
- [ ] Technical prerequisites are specific and achievable
- [ ] Capability prerequisites are clearly defined and measurable
- [ ] Implementation phases are logical and manageable
- [ ] Each phase includes objectives, activities, deliverables, and success criteria
- [ ] Critical success factors are essential and actionable
- [ ] Success factors include description, importance, implementation, and measurement
page_texts.10:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#practical-application]

### Practical Application

- [ ] Implementation steps are detailed and actionable
- [ ] Steps are logically sequenced and build upon each other
- [ ] Each step includes inputs, activities, outputs, and quality criteria
- [ ] Tools and techniques are appropriate and accessible
- [ ] Tool recommendations include purpose, usage guidelines, and cost information
- [ ] Techniques are proven and practical for the practice context
- [ ] Templates and artifacts are useful and complete
- [ ] Common pitfalls are realistic and well-documented
- [ ] Pitfall prevention and mitigation strategies are practical
- [ ] Implementation guidance enables successful adoption
page_texts.11:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#measurement-and-validation]

### Measurement and Validation

- [ ] Success metrics are comprehensive and measurable
- [ ] Business metrics demonstrate clear organizational value
- [ ] Technical metrics validate practice implementation effectiveness
- [ ] Process metrics ensure systematic implementation and operation
- [ ] Validation approaches are practical and comprehensive
- [ ] Validation methods include purpose, approach, criteria, and stakeholders
- [ ] Maturity assessment framework is logical and progressive
- [ ] Maturity levels are clearly differentiated and assessable
- [ ] Continuous improvement approach is systematic and sustainable
- [ ] Measurement approach enables ongoing optimization
page_texts.13:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#implementation-evidence]

### Implementation Evidence

- [ ] Best practice demonstrates proven effectiveness across multiple implementations
- [ ] Implementation history shows adequate validation period (minimum 6 months)
- [ ] Scale and scope of implementations demonstrate broad applicability
- [ ] Success evidence is credible and well-documented
- [ ] Quantified outcomes are realistic and achievable
- [ ] Evidence sources are authoritative and verifiable
- [ ] Implementation examples represent diverse contexts and organizations
- [ ] Results demonstrate consistent benefits across implementations
page_texts.14:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#examples-and-case-studies]

### Examples and Case Studies

- [ ] Examples are realistic and representative of typical implementations
- [ ] Case studies demonstrate comprehensive implementation and results
- [ ] Each example includes context, challenge, implementation, and outcomes
- [ ] Outcomes are quantified and credible
- [ ] Lessons learned are actionable and transferable
- [ ] Success stories demonstrate exceptional results and recognition
- [ ] Examples cover diverse organizational contexts and industries
- [ ] Case studies provide sufficient detail for replication
page_texts.15:
[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#expert-validation]

### Expert Validation

- [ ] Best practice has been reviewed by recognized subject matter experts
- [ ] Expert reviewers have demonstrated competency in the practice domain
- [ ] Expert feedback has been incorporated and addressed
- [ ] Multiple experts have validated the practice effectiveness
- [ ] Expert consensus supports practice recommendations and approach
- [ ] Expert validation covers both theoretical soundness and practical applicability
- [ ] Reviewers represent diverse perspectives and organizations
- [ ] Expert endorsement is documented and authoritative

[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#content-accuracy-and-currency]

### Content Accuracy and Currency

- [ ] All technical information is accurate and current
- [ ] References to external standards and frameworks are up-to-date
- [ ] Technology recommendations reflect current best practices
- [ ] Information is consistent throughout the document
- [ ] Data and statistics are from credible sources
- [ ] Industry trends and developments are accurately reflected
- [ ] Practice recommendations align with current technology evolution
- [ ] Content has been fact-checked and validated

[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#writing-quality-and-clarity]

### Writing Quality and Clarity

- [ ] Language is clear, professional, and appropriate for target audience
- [ ] Technical terms are properly defined and used consistently
- [ ] Grammar, spelling, and punctuation are correct
- [ ] Sentences are clear and concise
- [ ] Content flow is logical and easy to follow
- [ ] Voice and tone are consistent throughout

- [ ] Document follows enterprise architecture documentation standards
- [ ] Markdown formatting is consistent and correct
- [ ] File naming convention is followed correctly
- [ ] Directory structure follows established patterns

- [ ] Tables are properly formatted and readable

[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#enterprise-architecture-integration]

### Enterprise Architecture Integration

- [ ] Best practice aligns with enterprise architecture principles
- [ ] Relationships to standards (STD-{DOMAIN}-{TYPE}-{NNN}) are clearly documented and accurate
- [ ] Pattern relationships (PTN-{DOMAIN}-{SUBSECTION}-{###}) are relevant and beneficial
- [ ] Guidance connections (GUID-{DOMAIN}-{TYPE}-{NNN}) are appropriate and useful
- [ ] Reference architecture connections (REF-{DOMAIN}-{TYPE}-{NNN}) are appropriate and useful
- [ ] Dependencies on other practices, standards, patterns, and guidance are clearly identified
- [ ] All cross-references use correct ID formats for their artifact type
- [ ] Integration guidance enables effective implementation within enterprise context
- [ ] Practice supports enterprise architecture objectives and strategy
- [ ] Alignment with architectural governance is documented

[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#organizational-alignment]

### Organizational Alignment

- [ ] Practice supports organizational strategy and objectives
- [ ] Business value proposition is compelling and credible
- [ ] Practice aligns with organizational culture and capabilities
- [ ] Implementation approach considers organizational context and constraints
- [ ] Change management considerations are addressed
- [ ] Resource requirements are realistic and achievable
- [ ] Practice adoption fits within organizational change capacity

[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#industry-alignment]

### Industry Alignment

- [ ] Practice reflects current industry best practices and trends
- [ ] Approach is consistent with recognized industry frameworks
- [ ] Recommendations align with regulatory and compliance requirements
- [ ] Practice supports industry evolution and innovation
- [ ] External references are authoritative and current
- [ ] Industry case studies and examples are relevant and credible

[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#review-process-compliance]

- [ ] Best practice has undergone required review processes

[strategy/best-practices/best-practice-quality-checklist.md#checklist-usage-instructions]

## Checklist Usage Instructions

1. **Complete systematically** - Work through each section in order
2. **Document evidence** - Maintain evidence for each checklist item
3. **Address all items** - No items may be marked N/A or skipped
4. **Involve stakeholders** - Ensure appropriate stakeholder participation
5. **Iterate as needed** - Return to previous steps if issues are identified
6. **Maintain documentation** - Keep complete records of review process
7. **Obtain required approvals** - Ensure all necessary stakeholders have approved
8. **Update status** - Maintain current status throughout review process
